workflow.name: Public CCXT quickstart acceptance
workflow.scope: Linux release wheel and bundled CLI; public read-only 30-day 1h perpetual OHLCV; public default fees; backtest; HTML report. No credentials, private API calls, or orders. The workflow conclusion is failure only because Binance public exchangeInfo returned HTTP 451; OKX and Bitget jobs passed all quickstart assertions.

exchange_results.message: api.binance.com/api/v3/exchangeInfo returned a restricted-location eligibility response on the hosted runner

interpretation: This proves the Linux bundled install, public-data quickstart, backtest, report generation, and zero-rejection order admission for the tested OKX and Bitget paths. The previous Bitget run rejected 46 legacy market orders; the current run uses the same 720-bar quickstart scope and passes with 38 fills and zero rejections.
It does not prove private authenticated requests, testnet order execution, live trading, or strategy profitability. The reported returns are sample results, not evidence of strategy quality.
Binance remains unverified by this runner because its public market endpoint denied access by region; this evidence must not be used to bypass that restriction.
